subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack `message_changed` and `message_deleted` be suppressible before session wake, and should that be an opt-in config key, a default behavior change, or no change?
rationale: The source-level issue is real, but the requested fix creates a new public channel config surface and intersects with intentional system-event behavior plus the newer Assistant DM edit path.

options.title: Add opt-in Slack config
options.body: Add a narrowly typed `ignoreSubtypes`-style Slack config option that defaults to current behavior and preserves Assistant DM `message_changed` handling.

options.title: Change default policy
options.body: Drop ordinary edit/delete system events by default, with tests and docs explaining the intentional behavior shift for existing Slack users.

options.title: Keep system events
options.body: Leave edits/deletes as system events and document prompt or agent-level filtering as the supported policy.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in Slack config
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly typed `ignoreSubtypes`-style Slack config option that defaults to current behavior and preserves Assistant DM `message_changed` handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant Slack subtype behavior and adjacent thread-broadcast decision are most strongly tied to this history.
